title: Rep. Nancy Mace’s ex-fiancé and two others charged with sexual misconduct-related offenses | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

Three men whom US Rep. Nancy Mace accused of being “PREDATORS” in anunprecedented House floor speechlast year – including her ex-fiancé – were charged with sexual misconduct-related offenses Wednesday, the South Carolina Law Enforcement Division said in a statement.

Brendan Patrick Bryant, 53, Mace’s ex-fiancé, was charged with voyeurism. John Douglas Osborne, 46, was charged with first-degree assault and battery and two counts of third-degree criminal sexual conduct. Eric Bernard Bowman, 46, was charged with voyeurism, obstruction of justice and publishing the name of a victim of criminal sexual conduct, the agency said.

The three were charged in Charleston County and were booked into the Sheriff Al Cannon Detention Center, the agency said. The case will be prosecuted by the 9th Circuit Solicitor’s Office.

Bryant, Osborne and Bowman have posted bond and have been released from the detention center, according to Osborne’s attorney.

The affidavits allege that in October 2018 Osborne “unlawfully committed a sexual battery” against a 23-year-old woman who had “passed out” from alcohol use, while Bowman and Bryant “appear to take photographs and/or video of the Victim.”

The documents state an unnamed witness who was “watching a home security video feed … observed the incident,” obtained two still photos from the feed and wrote “an email/journal entry detailing the incident from her perspective.”

Bryant’s attorney told CNN on Wednesday Bryant “adamantly denies” the allegations and said he believes the “case should be contested and presented in the courtroom.”

The attorney also said Mace’s House floor speech “was full of falsehoods and blatant inconsistencies and Bryant adamantly denies any merit to any of those allegations and accusations.”

Osborne’s attorneys issued a statement Wednesday saying he “is innocent of the charges brought against him and intends to defend himself vigorously.”

CNN reached out to Bowman’s attorneys but did not immediately hear back. Last year,Bowman told CNN“no wrongdoing has been committed.”

The charges come more than a year after Mace, the Republican congresswoman from South Carolina,delivered a remarkable 53-minute speechon the House floor. After swearing on a Bible to tell the “whole truth,” she accused Bryant of “evil” crimes, including rape, and accused him and three other men of recording sex acts without consent. She displayed their names, photos and hometowns on a placard under an all-caps “PREDATORS.”

“Mr. Speaker, I rise today to call out the cowards who think they can prey on women and get away with it,” she said in February 2025. “Today, I’m going scorched earth.”

In her speech, Mace alleged she found more than 10,000 hidden camera videos and photos on Bryant’s phone in November 2023. She said she had spent the past year “searching for victims” and “uncovered” assaults that spanned “over a decade, almost 20 years.”

Mace did not provide specific evidence of her claims, but she said she brought the case to state authorities for further investigation. TheConstitution’s Speech or Debate Clausegenerally protects speech on the House floor from libel laws.

At the time,Bryant’s representativesent CNN a statement denying all “criminal allegations.”

The speech was just one of a number of noteworthy moments for Mace, an outspoken political figure who has served in Congress since 2021.

She shared anemotional accountof being raped as a teenager in a debate about an abortion bill in the South Carolina legislature before being elected to Congress. In her time in office, she has repeatedly sparked controversy bycriticizingbut thenendorsing President Donald Trump,picking personal feuds with colleagues, clashing with the presidentover the release of theJeffrey Epstein filesandallegedly berating officers at an airport.

This election cycle, she ran for governor of South Carolina but finished adisappointing fifthin the Republican primary.

CNN reached out Wednesday to Mace, who hasproposed legislationaffirming “her commitment to protecting women and standing with survivors by advancing legislation to strengthen victims’ rights and hold sexual predators accountable.”

Marybeth Mullaney, an attorney for the then-23-year-old woman, shared the woman’s victim impact statement that was read aloud in court at the men’s bond hearing Wednesday. In the statement, the woman said she did not know what happened to her that night and only learned she had been sexually assaulted in April 2024.

“Since then, my sense of safety, privacy, and trust has been shattered. I constantly worry about being watched, followed, or secretly recorded,” she said.

She said her experience, and cases like the alleged 2024 gang rape atCornell University, show the difficulty of holding powerful people and institutions accountable.

“I know this is only the first step toward these men taking accountability for what they did to me but it is a very significant step. All I wanted was the truth, the freedom to speak it, and the ability to live without fear,” she said.

One of the four men Mace named in her speech, Brian Musgrave, has not been charged. He denied wrongdoing in aninterview with CNNlast year, and his attorneys issued a statement Wednesday saying he and his family have “endured unimaginable distress and financial loss” since Mace “recklessly” accused him of significant sexual crimes.

“Obviously, Brian is happy not to have been criminally charged and not to be grouped with the others recently charged but it has opened up some pretty deep wounds,” attorneys Eric S. Bland and Ronald L. Richter Jr. said. “To this day Ms. Mace has never apologized to Brian and his family for what she falsely said about him. Quite frankly, she should have cleared his name long ago.”

The assault allegedly occurred in the early morning hours of October 26, 2018, at a house on Sullivan’s Island, South Carolina, according to court documents.

The victim, a 23-year-old woman, had consumed alcohol and was “so intoxicated she fell into the swimming pool” and was “unable to walk normally or speak cogently,” the documents state. She “passed out” on a sofa in the house, and while she was unconscious, Bryant, Osborne and Bowman agreed that Osborne would have sex with her, the court documents state.

Osborne then allegedly sexually assaulted her even though he “knew or should have known the Victim was unable to and did not provide consent,” the documents state. Bryant and Bowman “watched for the purpose of arousing or gratifying sexual desire,” the documents state.

In addition, Bowman faces charges of obstruction of justice and publishing the name of a victim of criminal sexual conduct dating to March 2025, weeks after Mace’s speech.

He allegedly did a “’factory’ reset” of his cellphone on March 23, 2025, just three days after South Carolina Law Enforcement Division agents executed a search warrant seeking the device and three days before he turned over his phone, according to court documents. In addition, he “did knowingly publish or cause to be published” the name of a woman the agency was investigating as an alleged victim of criminal sexual conduct on the social media platform X, the documents state.

CNN’s Sarah Ferris contributed to this report.

CNN’s Sarah Ferris contributed to this report.
